facts.text: Cherokee holds National Historic Landmark status, recognizing its rich historical significance in the state of Iowa.
Cherokee was laid out in 1870 and named after the Southeast Indian tribe whose members were relocated to Indian Territory in the 1830s.
The original Cherokee, later called Old Cherokee, was founded in December 1857 north of the current county seat beside the Little Sioux River.
The story of Sioux Chief Inkpaduta and the events leading to the Spirit Lake Massacre is a colorful chapter in Cherokee history.
A promised railroad from Fort Dodge to Sioux City through Cherokee attracted businesses in the late 1860s, but when completed in 1870 it missed the Little Sioux River.
Cherokee was officially incorporated on April 5, 1873, solidifying its status as the county seat.
